subject: Procurement decision: invoicing, SLA credits, and contract gating (marketplace vs direct)
messages:
From: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@acme-telecom.com>

Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Procurement question: invoicing & SLA credits — marketplace or direct?

Hi Soojin,

Quick intro — I'm Priya on Acme Telecom's procurement team. We're evaluating Redwood for a pilot (internal app team) and trying to decide whether to transact via AWS Marketplace (quick PO, easier billing) or pursue a direct contract / MSA with Redwood. A few questions came up from legal and finance: 

- If we buy via marketplace, who is the contracting party for SLA credits and indemnities? Will Redwood still honor SLA credits even though invoice comes from AWS?
- How are invoice timing and payment terms different between marketplace vs direct? Net 30 vs marketplace immediate charge?
- For audit evidence (SOC2, KMS details), can we get those the same way for marketplace purchases?
- If we later want seat-based reserved capacity under a Reserved Capacity agreement, can we switch from marketplace to direct mid-term without interruption?

We'd like a short one-pager we can share with finance & legal that calls out pros/cons and typical timelines. Can you and your team help?

Thanks,
Priya Sharma
Procurement Manager, Acme Telecom
priya.sharma@acme-telecom.com

Subject: Re: Procurement question: invoicing & SLA credits — marketplace or direct?

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear list. Short summary up front: both routes are supported; marketplace is fastest to get started and simpler for procurement, direct (MSA + SOW) gives you full contract terms, flexible billing, and direct SLA remedies. I've attached a one-pager and an example MSA redline to this thread.

High-level answers to your bullets:

- Contracting party & SLA credits:
  - Marketplace: AWS is the billing/ordering entity; Redwood remains the service provider. We will honor SLA credits per our published SLA but administrative assignment of credits is typically coordinated through Redwood and AWS. For large credit claims or escalations, we engage directly with AWS marketplace invoicing teams.
  - Direct: Redwood is the contracting party and credits are handled directly under the MSA; faster path for credit application and bulk remedies.

- Invoice timing & payment terms:
  - Marketplace: Procures are usually charged on AWS billing cycles. Payment flows to AWS, and you reconcile via your AWS bill. Marketplace line items appear on the monthly AWS invoice — payment term is whatever you have with AWS (often Net 30 depending on your AWS agreement).
  - Direct: Redwood issues invoices per the agreed SOW schedule (monthly, quarterly, or upfront). We typically support Net 30 for enterprise customers, or custom terms per deal.

- Audit evidence / compliance docs:
  - Marketplace: We can provide SOC2 reports, architecture diagrams, and KMS integration notes regardless of buying channel. However, some customers prefer direct contracts for additional data handling clauses or to attach DPA language directly to Redwood's MSA.

- Moving from marketplace to direct mid-term:
  - Possible but requires coordination: typically you'd sign an MSA and we migrate billing. We plan migrations to avoid service interruption; there is an operational window to move entitlements and reserved capacity. Timing depends on AWS transfer windows and whether Reserved Capacity was purchased via marketplace SKU or direct reservation.

Next steps we recommend:
- I uploaded a short one-pager (attached) that finance/legal can review.
- Vanessa (cc) can confirm standard net terms and any one-time onboarding credits for marketplace pilots.
- If legal wants to start redlines, I attached an example MSA with common redline positions.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call with procurement and legal to walk through — are you available Wed or Thu?

Best,

Subject: Re: Procurement question: invoicing & SLA credits — marketplace or direct?

Hi Priya,

Appreciate the questions. A couple of operational clarifications from finance/sales ops: 

- Pilot via Marketplace: we can offer a trial credit for the first 30 days and typically do not require an MSA to start. Invoices will show up on your AWS bill; internal chargeback to your team is straightforward.
- Direct purchase: if you want Reserved Capacity and committed monthly spend with invoicing from Redwood, we can issue a PO-based invoice and support Net 30. Switching mid-contract is supported but requires a migration ticket and EA (entitlement assignment) time (~5-10 business days typically).

On SLA credits, practical note: for small pilot incidents marketplace refunds often go through AWS which can add latency to getting credit applied. For production SLAs (financial credits > $X), Redwood's direct MSA route is faster.

If legal shares redlines, our legal team will prioritize when they see an active deal in HubSpot (link below). To speed review, put the HubSpot deal ID in the redline email.

HubSpot Deal: https://hubspot.redwood.company/deal/DEAL-9831
